ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, managers, and signatories against the Luxembourg FIU (Cellule de Renseignement Financier) national list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, and global PEP databases covering family members and close associates. Applies FATF Recommendations 12, 22, and 25 and Article 5 of the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for foreign PEPs, source-of-funds verification is required for Apple IAP / Google Play billing rails, and continuous monitoring with negative news screening is required at least annually; 100% of UBOs and appointees must be screened before the notarial deed is passed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) — official portal https://www.lbr.lu and search interface at https://r.cs.lu (operated pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002 and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 August 2015)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory requirement that the corporate name be written in Latin script and expressed in one of the working languages of Luxembourg (Luxembourgish, French, German or, by RCS practice, English). Non-Latin script names (e.g., Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic) are not accepted as the statutory corporate name; a transliterated or translated Latin-script version must be adopted, and the full corporate name must include the legal form 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'S.à r.l.' / 'SARL' with the full wording set out in the articles of association.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Casino / Jeux de hasard / Gaming House / Jackpot
Luxembourg / Lëtzebuerg (where it misleadingly suggests state sponsorship)
Union européenne / European Union / UE / EU / NATO / UN
Chambre de commerce / Chamber of Commerce
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In case of name rejection, the applicant may request a reasoned re-examination by written application to the RCS registration department within 15 days of the rejection notice, attaching a negative preliminary trademark search report from the Luxembourg Intellectual Property Office and an explanation of distinctiveness. If the RCS maintains refusal, a formal administrative appeal must be filed with the Tribunal administratif (Luxembourg City) within three months of notification pursuant to the amended Law of 1 December 1978 on non-contentious procedure; the appeal brief must assert compliance with Article 1er of the Law of 19 December 2002 and the naming requirements of the Companies Law of 10 August 1915, and may request interim suspension of the contested decision. A rejected name may be re-filed in amended form immediately.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted virtual-office acceptance: the SARL must maintain a registered office at a real physical address in Luxembourg capable of receiving service of process; a mailbox-only virtual office is impermissible. A regulated domiciliation agent (agréé under the Law of 16 May 2019) may provide the registered seat, but this is accepted by the RCS and tax authorities only where the company has genuine local substance (management decisions, records, or activities). For ISIC 5820 digital social-casino publishing with solely cross-border IAP revenue, reliance on a pure virtual office materially raises the risk of substance challenge (permanent establishment/directorate issues) and potential denial of double-taxation treaty benefits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: ~35% probability within the first 24 months after incorporation: unannounced physical on-site checks may be conducted by the Luxembourg direct tax administration (Administration des contributions directes), the RCS/court bailiffs, and social security authorities to verify commercial substance; inspection likelihood is elevated for foreign-owned SARLs with no resident employees and Apple/Google billing-derived revenue streams, while CSSF inspections are not applicable to this unregulated software publisher.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Title VII, Articles 710-1 to 710-26 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée); Amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and Business Accounting (RCS Law); Law of 2 September 2011 on Access to the Professions of Craftsman, Trader, and Industrialist.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) de Luxembourg, operating under the authority of the Ministry of Justice; electronic filings via the LBR and Guichet.lu portals.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (acte constitutif) embodying the Articles of Association (statuts), executed before a Luxembourg notary, followed by mandatory RCS registration and publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Standard SARL minimum share capital: EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up at incorporation; alternatively, under Article 710-17 of the 1915 Law, capital may be set below EUR 12,000 but not below EUR 1, cash contributions only, subject to statutory reserve and profit-distribution restrictions for the first five years. Cash contributions must be deposited on a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) with a credit institution in Luxembourg or another EU/EEA state and the bank's blocking certificate delivered to the notary before execution of the deed; in-kind contributions require a valuation report by an approved réviseur d'entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The formation of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée under Luxembourg law, with the corporate name set out in the articles of association, is approved; (2) the subscription and allocation of share capital among the founding members and the blocking of funds on a dedicated escrow account are ratified; (3) the registered office is fixed at the address of the registered corporate services provider; (4) [Name] is appointed manager (gérant) with sole-signature power and [Name] is appointed compliance officer; (5) the manager is authorized to execute the notarial deed, complete the RCS filing, and undertake all establishment-permit, tax, and bank-account formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Search and Negative Certificate (Certificat de Non-Confusion)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS) via the LBR electronic portal or Guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a preliminary online feasibility search for at least two proposed names incorporating the suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL'. Submit the formal reservation/search request to LBR and obtain the negative certificate confirming that the chosen name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered corporate name or protected trademark. Deliver the negative certificate to the notary for insertion in the deed.
required_dossiers: Copy of valid national ID or passport of each founding member
Bank confirmation letter or mandate (if requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as confusing, file an objection through the notary, submit a curative alternative name within the reservation period, or appeal a definitive refusal to the Director of LBR and subsequently to the administrative tribunal within three months.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes (portal: impotsdirects.public.lu) and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT (portal: aedt.public.lu); unified state e-services portal: guichet.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: incorporate SARL before a notary and file with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); the RCS company number serves as the national identification number for the legal entity. Step 2: ACD automatically opens the corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and municipal business tax file and issues the e-file access (eCDF). Step 3: receive the AEDT VAT file and Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits) by filing the VAT registration form (formulaire TVA) via the guichet.public.lu e-space before the first taxable transaction. Non-resident foreign entities establishing a branch follow the same RCS then VAT registration sequence; there is no de minimis threshold for non-residents unless they use the EU OSS or reverse charge mechanism. Standard processing time is 2-4 weeks after submission of the certified statutes, certificate of residence of managers, and power of attorney.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the resident SARL is independently taxable on worldwide income with tax transparency disallowed; profits are taxed at the corporate level and distributions are subject to a 15% withholding tax (reduced to 0% under the participation exemption); branch-level territorial sourcing applies only to non-resident taxpayers. The entity is outside any tax-exempt zone regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. Relevant statutory mechanisms include: (i) fiscal unity/group taxation election for corporate income tax and municipal business tax effective from tax year 2025 (95% ownership threshold), (ii) VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, (iii) automatic application of the participation exemption (no election required if the 10% holding / EUR 1.2 million cost and 12-month holding conditions are met), and (iv) mandatory, non-elective hybrid mismatch adjustments under the ATAD implementation law of 21 December 2018.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA), governed by the amended Law of 12 February 1979
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover (excl. VAT) for the resident small-business exemption (Article 57 VAT Law); EUR 10,000 EU-wide annual threshold for B2C e-services/distance sales below which Luxembourg VAT applies locally and above which the OSS returns are used; no registration threshold whatsoever for non-resident suppliers of taxable goods or services in Luxembourg outside OSS/reverse charge.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg imposes no general real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory continuous transaction control (CTC) API clearance, and no digital stamping for B2B/B2C invoices. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing via PEPPOL is phased in: central state entities from 1 January 2024 and all public contracting authorities from 1 January 2025. B2B e-invoicing is voluntary and consensual (PDF, EDI, PEPPOL or XML accepted). VAT returns and the EuC3 / recapitulative statements must be filed electronically through the eCDF portal; OSS returns are filed quarterly on the national OSS portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% rate applies to (i) intra-Community supplies of goods to a customer holding a valid EU VAT identification number and (ii) exports of goods outside the EU evidenced by an accepted customs export declaration. For the target activity (simulated social casino and virtual slots software distributed via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing), supplies are electronically supplied services: B2B supplies are reverse-charged to the business customer and B2C supplies are declared in the customer's EU member state via OSS; consequently no Luxembourg output VAT is triggered and no export zero-rating claim is needed unless software is exported on physical media, in which case the export documentation bundle below applies. Input VAT on domestic costs is creditable or refundable by the AEDT within the ordinary rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EX-A) with electronic acceptance reference IE-529 evidencing dispatch outside the EU
Bill of Lading, airway bill, or CMR consignment note bearing the consignee's signature as transport evidence
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment statement showing receipt of export consideration within 180 days
Commercial invoice, purchase order/contract, and customer proof of EU-VAT-ID where intra-Community supply is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may reassess zero-rated exports within the standard 5-year limitation period, extended to 10 years in case of fraud or omission. Unsubstantiated export zero-rating is clawed back at 17% VAT with late-payment interest accruing at 0.6% per month; administrative fines are imposed under Article 671 et seq. of the Luxembourg General Tax Code (A.O.), and intentional or reckless claims constitute VAT fraud punishable by imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years and/or fines up to EUR 25,000 (or twice the evaded tax). OSS misdeclarations trigger analogous reassessment through the OSS portal with automatic information exchange to the member state of consumption.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), as the Eurosystem national central bank, holds monetary policy execution, foreign exchange reserves and balance-of-payments statistics. The Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises credit institutions, payment institutions, e-money institutions and enforces AML/CFT under the Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing and CSSF Regulation 12-02. Significant banks fall under the ECB Single Supervisory Mechanism. Payment services are regulated under the Law of 10 November 2009 transposing PSD2; e-money issuers are regulated under the Law of 20 December 2019. The Ministry of Finance has no direct casino-gaming licensing competence because the SARL's activity is non-gambling software publishing (ISIC 5820) outside the scope of the Law of 19 December 2022 on betting and gaming.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility in both current and capital accounts. As a Eurozone member applying TFEU Article 63, Luxembourg imposes no exchange controls, no pre-authorisation for capital movements, and no restrictions on dividend, interest, royalty or capital repatriation. EUR is the domestic legal tender, but foreign-currency accounts are freely admitted for corporate treasuries. Remittance frictions are fiscal rather than monetary: 15% dividend withholding tax (0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive when a 10% participation is held for at least 12 months; reduced treaty rates apply) and 10% withholding on certain royalty outflows unless treaty-relieved. BCL statistical reporting applies to cross-border transactions above EUR 12,500 per item or EUR 50,000 per counterparty per year, submitted monthly via the BP6 web-portal; no central-bank approval is ever required to open a bank account or to move gaming-software revenues into Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export-proceeds surrender obligations, mandatory conversion ratios or holding-period restrictions apply in Luxembourg. Receipts from Apple/Google storefronts, sub-publishers and international licensees may be retained indefinitely in USD or any convertible currency without repatriation schedules. Statutory duties are limited to: (i) BCL BP6 monthly balance-of-payments declarations for cross-border credits/debits above the EUR 12,500/50,000 thresholds, capturing ISIC 5820 software royalties and in-app-purchase settlements; (ii) CSSF AML/CFT suspicious-transaction reporting; (iii) standard banking provenance checks requiring the company to hold the underlying merchant settlement statements and export invoices on file. There is no surrendering institution, and no conversion into EUR is mandated for any trade flow.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account - multi-currency EUR/USD; Capital Escrow Account for statutory minimum capital deposit
Operational Account - EUR/USD; Capital Escrow Account; dedicated merchant-collections account for Apple/Google settlements
Operational Account - corporate treasury, SWIFT-cleared transfers, FX line
Operational Account - domestic and SEPA disbursements; limited digital onboarding
Operational Account - private-banking and ultra-high-net-worth only; unsuitable for treasury-execution volume

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a complementary multi-currency payment overlay; Low as the sole treasury-banking solution. Luxembourg-regulated EMIs, notably MANGOPAY S.A. and PayTech Luxembourg S.A., plus EU-passported institutions such as Adyen N.V., can lawfully open payment accounts for the SARL, collect App-Store flows and automate virtual-card payouts to sub-licensees. Legal constraints under PSD2/EMD2 include: no credit intermediation or overdraft, no proprietary FX derivative execution, mandatory segregation of client funds into a Tier-1 Luxembourg credit institution, and prohibition on issuing capital-escrow confirmations for notarial SARL capitalisation. EMIs domiciled outside the EEA without an EU passport are not viable because they cannot offer EUR-denominated payment accounts inside Luxembourg without breaching the Law of 10 November 2009. Recommended operating model: maintain the primary operating and statutory capital accounts at a Tier-1 bank, and deploy one CSSF-authorised EMI solely for high-frequency payment-account automation, treasury data aggregation and commercial-card distributions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg statutory law does not mandate a physical appearance; CSSF Circular 19/705 permits remote client identification via an eIDAS-compliant electronic signature or an audited video-KYC procedure with cross-verification against independent official databases. Notwithstanding the legal permissiveness, the observable onboarding practice for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced ISIC 5820 merchant with non-resident UBOs requires at least one in-branch interview at the chosen Tier-1 bank: the resident Manager (Gerant) and the ultimate beneficial owner must appear physically with passports, proof of residential address, source-of-wealth documentation and original corporate file extracts. A CSSF-approved fiduciary, notary or a Luxembourg statutory auditor may act as introducer to mitigate friction, but a fully remote opening is realistically not available. Domestic substance requirements are satisfied through a contracted registered office and a Luxembourg-resident professional director if needed, preserving the SARL's tax and corporate compliance posture.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Keyword-based bank screening classifies 'casino' or 'slots' nomenclature as regulated gambling, triggering automatic industry-exclusion and an immediate SAR-referral.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier bundle: legal opinion, storefront agreements, terms-of-service, game-design documentation, ministry confirmation letter, and a management sworn declaration distinguishing ISIC 5820 from gambling activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-Luxembourg UBO chain without independently verifiable source-of-wealth, triggering enhanced due diligence under CSSF Circular 20/06.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RBE register extract, certified corporate chart of the entire ownership chain, three years of audited financial statements or equivalent tax returns for each UBO, bank references from the existing primary bank, notarised source-of-wealth statements and tax-residency certificates (form 6166) for each qualifying beneficial owner, all apostilled and translated into French/German/English as required by the onboarding bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Atypical transactional profile: thousands of sub-EUR 10 virtual-chip micro-purchases flowing into the SARL as monthly, USD-denominated merchant settlements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly App Store Connect and Google Play Console settlement statements, server-to-server purchase-verification receipts, a live virtual-chips consumption ledger, bank-matched reconciliation pack per settlement cycle, onboarded PCI-DSS report of compliance, and the VAT cluster registrations proving EU-wide reporting of each digital sale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Geographic-risk flags because the game is available in FATF-listed, financially sanctioned or non-cooperative jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Controlled territorial-distribution settings in the App Store/Play Console excluding sanctioned jurisdictions; written policy of Apple/Google acting as merchant of record insulating the SARL from buyer-side exposure; negative-media screening reports from World-Check or Dow Jones; a group AML/CFT procedure naming the appointed responsible person and stating geo-IP blocking thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty disbursements to non-resident sub-publishers and game-development studios mischaracterised as transaction-laundering or profit-stripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed publisher, licensing and milestone-development agreements with mathematical royalty formulas; settlement computation sheets per counterparty per quarter; transfer-pricing documentation (local-file or simplified benchmark study) demonstrating arm's-length pricing; invoice-to-wire matching records; and, if required, a Luxembourg withholding tax certificate showing the correct treaty treatment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections must arrive as SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA CT in EUR) to the SARL's named IBAN at the Tier-1 bank. For the statutory minimum capital of EUR 12,000 required by Article 710-13 of the Law of 10 August 1915, the bank's account officer must issue a blocked-funds certificate (attestation de blocage) on the capital-escrow account before notarial execution of the articles of incorporation. Ongoing shareholder contributions must use balance-of-payments purpose code S0301 (equity capital other than investment fund shares) in MT103 field 70 or 72; intercompany shareholder loans use S0202 (other loans). Apple/Google in-app-purchase proceeds arrive from the platform merchant-of-record through USD wire settlements referencing the operating agreement; the Treasury should instruct the bank to automatically match the ACH/SWIFT credit against the platform settlement reference and convert to EUR at the ECB reference rate when the hedging program mandates it. All inbound flows must reconcile to the monthly BCL BP6 declaration and to the statutory annual accounts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR disbursements, using purpose code ROYL for royalty/licence payments to foreign sub-publishers and INTC for related-party software-development fees, with mandatory field-70 invoice-reconciliation references; (ii) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and TARGET2 instant payments for EUR disbursements to EU vendors; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit are generally unsuitable for software publishing because delivery is electronic and no transport documents exist, except as a standby LC where a large milestone-staged development contract is in place and the counterparty demands bank security. Vendor payments for user-acquisition (Meta, TikTok, Google Ads) execute as MT103 in USD after a documented FX spot transaction; intra-group profit distributions follow the statutory dividend procedure and may be paid via SEPA or MT103 with reference to the tax annex. The virtual-coin model does not generate fiat outbound redemptions, which is a fundamental fact evidenced to banks to distinguish the company from real-money gaming operators.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD forward contracts, tenors up to 24 months, documented under an ISDA 2002 and Luxembourg Credit Support Deed with a CSSF-supervised counterparty, hedging the periodic app-store USD settlement flows.
EUR/USD cross-currency swaps aligned to notional Apple/Google quarterly revenue remittances, permitted for treasury-balance-sheet hedging under CSSF prudential standards.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on high-volatility emerging-market currencies (e.g., TRY, BRL, ZAR) where app-store local-currency pricing creates an identifiable residual exposure, provided the NDF counterparty is EU-regulated or a CSSF-recognised third-country bank under EMIR.
Zero-premium FX option collars (EUR/USD) to cap conversion-rate deterioration on peak-season revenue, permissible as an overlay hedge subject to MiFID II appropriateness classification.
Short-term EUR/USD forward outrights, 1-month or shorter tenors, executed as treasury-service line products under the bank's automated hedging mandate for monthly settlement-cycle swopping.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per calendar year; changes to beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days; no-change annual confirmation may be filed any time during the year, commonly aligned with the annual accounts filing cycle (7 months after financial year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 125,000 and imprisonment of 6 months to 2 years for defaulting managers; repeated non-confirmation may trigger judicial dissolution and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts and Statutory Financial Statements (comptes annuels) with auditor's report when applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after balance-sheet date; for a calendar-year SARL, no later than 31 July of the following financial year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers coercive daily fines (astreintes, typically EUR 250 per day), registration sanctions, and after formal notice administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax, Municipal Business Tax and Net Wealth Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SARL, file by 31 May of the following year; electronic submission may obtain an extension to 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing leads to default tax assessment, late-payment interest at 0.6% per month, and late-payment penalties of 10% to 30% of the additional tax due; persistent non-filing may entail enforced tax collection and company strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint an independent statutory auditor (reviseur d'entreprises agree) when it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds on two consecutive financial years: total balance sheet EUR 5,590,000; net turnover EUR 11,172,000; average number of employees 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Luxembourg law of 19 December 2002 and the Plan Comptable Normalise; consolidated accounts by large groups may elect IFRS as adopted by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must file an annual confirmation of UBO data at least once per calendar year even if no changes occurred. Any direct or indirect share transfer or beneficial-ownership change must be documented in the Register of Members and reported to the Luxembourg RBE within 30 days; the subsequent annual confirmation must certify that the register reflects the current ownership chain.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 4,500 per year for Luxembourg registered-office, domiciliation, and corporate secretarial agent services including RCS and RBE liaison.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 per year for a certified Luxembourg statutory audit when triggered; no audit fee is required below the statutory threshold.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% (plus 7% solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax, combined effective rate approx. 24.94% for Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), participation exemption for dividends and capital gains, notional interest deduction (NID) for equity financing, indefinite tax loss carryforward subject to anti-abuse rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1 (Corporate Income Tax Return) and Form 200 (Municipal Business Tax Return) filed via MyGuichet (electronic filing portal)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 31 May of the following year; extensions up to 31 December are commonly granted upon request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Luxembourg-source income only; apply treaty provisions if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions (business expenses, depreciation, IP box exemption, participation exemption)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only deductions directly related to Luxembourg-source income; maintain supporting documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (foreign tax credit, investment tax credit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Form 2 for foreign tax credit claims; provide TRC and proof of foreign taxes paid.
Ensure all adjustments are consistent with Luxembourg GAAP and tax rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: EUR 100 to EUR 1,000 per day, plus interest on unpaid tax at 0.5% per month. Additional penalties for inaccurate returns up to 10% of the tax due.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if holding >=10% for 12 months)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, submit a tax residency certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority and complete Form 2 (withholding tax exemption request) to the Luxembourg tax administration (ACD). The ACD typically processes within 3-6 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 0% (no WHT on interest). Royalties: 15% statutory, reduced to 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive if conditions hold, or under DTA rates (typically 0-10%).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 500 million group turnover for Master File; Local File required if related party transactions exceed EUR 1 million (goods) or EUR 100,000 (services).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Requirements (ESR) for entities engaged in IP holding, licensing, or leasing activities. For software publishing, substance is assessed by actual business activities, employees, and premises. A SARL must demonstrate real economic presence to avoid classification as a shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income or overstating deductions to reduce tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years, plus civil penalties of 10% to 200% of the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in fraud; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without real economic substance, such as no employees, no premises, or no actual business activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax benefits, recharacterization of income, and potential liquidation; fines up to EUR 1 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for tax debts if the company is deemed a shell; potential criminal liability for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement adequate anti-money laundering procedures, especially for high-risk gaming transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to EUR 5 million or 10% of annual turnover; suspension of operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal prosecution, imprisonment up to 5 years, and personal fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany prices that deviate from arm's length, leading to profit shifting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalties of 10% to 50% of the underpaid tax, and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for negligence if they failed to ensure proper TP documentation.
